a: Each node has two adjacent ✓ nodes to either side. The node holding the token can transmit data to ✓ other nodes. Data can only flow in one direction ✓. This avoids collisions ✓. Adding a new cable is relatively hard as an existing cable must be removed.

A peer-to-peer network has no central file server. Each computer is of equal status. Each computer can supply resources, consume resources and request resources. A client-server network has a dedicated computer acting as the central file server. The dedicated computer provides resources for all other dumb terminals/clients. Peer-to-peer requires much less hardware and software so it is a cheaper option suitable for small organisations. Client-server is more secure as all network resources are shared through a dedicated file computer.
note: Quality of written communication assessed: top band. Short, accurate and each point about one network is matched by a point about the other.

Presentation: Converts information/data to its correct audio/video format ✓. Compresses ✓/decompresses information. Includes encryption. Interacts with the ✓ application layer above and the session layer below.
Data Link: Deals with functions such as error detection ✓, error correction ✓, creating data blocks ✓ and synchronising data blocks. Splits outgoing data packets into a series of bits / a series of incoming bits into data packets. Interacts with the network layer above and the physical layer below.
The OSI model provides rules and standards that devices must follow to enable them to communicate/connect with other devices. ✗

TCP/IP: Dictates how data is packaged, sent and received. The TCP layer ✓ controls how data is packaged and the IP ✓ layer dictates how data is transferred from node to node and gives all devices a unique address.
Bluetooth: Enables devices to pair ✓ peer to peer. Creates an ad hoc network called a piconet ✓. The device wishing to pair will display all other bluetooth enabled devices within range given they are set to visible ✓. This may require a passcode. Has a range of 10m to 100m.
note: For TCP/IP, add the detail of what TCP does: splits data into numbered packets, checks they all arrive and reassembles them in order, requesting any lost packets again.

a: QBE is a graphical way of querying a database. The user enters commands into a blank template to specify the tables and fields to be used in a query. SQL is a programming language designed to create and manipulate databases. It provides a list of commands which can update, delete and create tables and queries. Each command has its own syntax. QBE is designed to generate queries and is much simpler requiring less IT expertise and knowledge. SQL requires high levels of IT expertise requiring the user to memorise syntax but it can be used to generate queries more efficiently than QBE.
note: Quality of written communication assessed. Good balance, but 'evaluate' needs a justified conclusion, e.g. 'QBE is the better choice for occasional users running simple queries, but SQL is needed for complex queries and for creating or changing the database structure.'

a: The Turing test aims to discover whether a machine's behaviour is indistinguishable from a human's response ✓. The test includes a player, human and machine ✓. The player does not know which is the human or machine ✓. The player asks questions of both and tries to determine ✓ which is the human. If the player is wrong, the machine has demonstrated human intelligence.

Shell: The software development ✓ environment for the creation of an expert system. Includes components of an ✓ expert system such as the knowledge ✓ base / inference engine. These can be populated for a particular application.
Fuzzy logic: Uses probabilities / degrees of truth rather than true and ✓ false / boolean logic. The computer mimics the human brain by using incomplete data to ✓ solve a problem by making the best possible solution given the input.
User interface: Asks the end user a series of questions and follow up questions ✓ regarding the subject domain. Uses the responses with the inference engine and knowledge base to calculate a response. May use a WIMP interface. Is user friendly. ✓
note: For the UI, say it presents the conclusion/advice to the user AND can explain how it was reached (the explanation facility). 'User friendly' earns nothing at A level.

The base station controller controls one or more base stations. They handle handover management. This is when a person making a call moves from one cell (a small hexagonal area containing a base station and mobile phone mast, strategically placed to provide maximum coverage) to another. The network provider automatically switches call responsibility from one base station to another. This is called a handoff. Base station controllers work with mobile switching centres to provide a public switched telephone network that enables mobile phones to make calls to other compatible devices such as a land line. Mobile phone masts use radio signals to operate phone calls.
note: Quality of written communication assessed: top band. All six terms used accurately.
